title: I Used the Ski-Rental Boot-Size Log on the Tech Who Swapped Pairs

parts.text: I clipped in at 8:40 a.m. and the boots were a 27.5 with my 26.5 still on the log. The rental log the tech initialed said: SIZE AS FITTED. NO SHOP SWAPS AFTER ISSUE. I was thirty-one, day pass, holding a blister already. Tech Gavin said, "We needed 26.5 for a VIP." I pointed at his initials. He shrugged. "VIPs are the mountain." I photographed the mismatch, the log, and the blister. Then I used the rental camera still of my fitting. At 8:47 the shop lead asked why Gavin's name was on a size-swap ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shop lead can see my 26.5 fitting still against a 27.5 on my feet.

social.video_title: He swapped my ski boots for a VIP — Part 1/2
social.description: Blister, a log he initialed, and a VIP excuse. I pulled the fitting still. Would you have skied sloppy?

parts.text: Gavin called it a shuffle until the still showed the VIP getting my pair. I printed the ticket, the log, and the photo. I got 26.5 back. Gavin told the bench the log was always about optics. Optics is a word techs use when a blister has a timestamp. Boot policy now has a second line: VIPS ARE NOT MY FEET. I ski true. Gavin fits VIPs from inventory. The liner finally matches the log.

social.video_title: VIPs are not my boot size — Part 2/2
social.description: Size-swap ticket, my 26.5 back, and a second line on the log. Was the mountain ever a shuffle?
